questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean the same way the operator leans.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean the same way. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle and makes it sit lower. Ride slower than usual, especially through curves and over bumps. The extra weight means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep a bigger space cushion between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Your main source of information about your motorcycle should be:
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual for information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light when:

options.text: You will be slowing down where other drivers won't expect it.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down in places drivers won't expect it, like the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly. Let off the gas and keep going straight. If you need to brake, slowly apply it only to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road. Squeeze the clutch and stop.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on dry pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on dry pavement, keep it locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will still be under control as long as it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: If you must brake in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve before braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning. Try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes slowly and gently.

questions.question: You should:

options.text: Shift gears while in a turn.
Shift gears before entering a turn.
Change power suddenly while in a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift gears before entering a turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn, not while you are in it.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Ride close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on at intersections. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see it clearly. Keep enough space between you and other vehicles so you can react to danger. Do not rely on eye contact alone to be noticed.

questions.question: To make a quick stop on wet pavement, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes if you need to stop quickly on wet pavement. Apply the front brake gradually to avoid locking it.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It works less well than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not give the same protection as goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: How long should a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: You do not need to do it before every ride.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: How should a group ride when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: How do you brake the shortest distance in a straight line?

options.text: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straightaway, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: What does it mean when you make eye contact with another driver?

options.text: The driver will definitely yield to you.
It is not worth your effort.
The driver may not properly yield to you.
The driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means the other driver will yield to you. Never count on it.

questions.question: Which choice is NOT a good way to increase your visibility?

options.text: Use your headlight at all times.

questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: Should you follow closer or farther away at night than during the day?

options.text: Keep the same distance day and night.

questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distance at night because you cannot see shadows and light contrasts. Allow a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: Where should a passenger ride on a motorcycle with a sidecar?

options.text: Either on the seat or in the sidecar.
Not on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, your passenger should ride in it. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar.

questions.question: How should you secure a load in a sidecar?

options.text: Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place it loose in the seat.
Secure it near the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in a sidecar so they do not move and affect how the motorcycle handles. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent tipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: What should you NOT do on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently. Do not brake quickly.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you also drink alcohol.
Have the same effect on all people.

questions.explanation: Many drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal) have side effects like alcohol. These side effects can make it harder to ride safely.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Practice on a quiet road first to get used to how your motorcycle feels with a passenger. The extra weight changes how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, it is best to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely and let them go in front of you. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips (less than five miles) at low speeds (under 30 mph).

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.
